newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Rabobank to cut back on new lending.
newsitem.headline: Rabobank to cut back on new lending.

text.p: Dutch co-operative bank Rabobank Nederland BA said on Monday it was reducing new lending to maintain its strong capitalisation levels.
Executive board chairman Herman Wijffels said growth in the business in the first half of 1996 was 50 percent above the normal level of about eight to nine percent per year.
"High credit growth also demands a lot of capital to finance it. We are now cutting back on giving new credits," he told Reuters.
The unlisted bank's loan portfolio grew 12.3 percent in the first half of 1996 to 209.4 billion guilders at June 30.
"In order to maintain our relatively strong capitalisation, we are cutting back on (loan) growth," he added.
He said that as Rabobank was not listed and had no plans in the foreseeable future to seek a share market listing, it preferred to finance its growth internally.
Rabobank was cutting back lending growth by syndicating loans to other banks and increasing interest margins on loans.
"We have the impression that some of our colleagues are in the same sitatuion," Wijffels said.
Rabobank is the biggest lender to small and medium-sized businesses and biggest mortgage provider in the Netherlands.
But it ranks behind ABN AMRO and Internationale Nederlanden Groep NV in corporate lending in the Netherlands.

Rabobank's capital adequacy ratio eased to 11.5 percent at June 30 from 11.9 percent a year ago due partly to the sharp rise in lending, but it remained above the minimum eight percent level specified by the Bank for International Settlements.
The bank's new mortgage loans grew by 50 percent in the first half due to a strong domestic housing market but Wijffels said he believed house prices were nearing their peak.
